title: A New Approach to Linear Filtering and Prediction Problems
abstract: The classical filtering problem is treated from the viewpoint of state-space theory. A recursive solution is developed that is ideally suited for digital computation. The filter uses physical kinematic state equations and statistical measurement updates to produce the minimum mean-square error estimate.
sample_notes:
# Field Derivation Notes: State Estimation in Noisy Terrains

Problem Statement:
Autonomous drone navigating high-vibration environment. GPS sample rate 10Hz with sigma=1.5m, IMU drift rate 0.05m/s^2.
How to estimate true velocity and position?

Dynamics:
$x_{k} = A x_{k-1} + B u_k + w_k$
Measurement:
$z_k = H x_k + v_k$

Assume $w_k \sim \mathcal{N}(0, Q)$, $v_k \sim \mathcal{N}(0, R)$.

Prior State Predict:
$\hat{x}_k^- = A \hat{x}_{k-1}$
$P_k^- = A P_{k-1} A^T + Q$

Kalman Gain Derivation:
$K_k = P_k^- H^T (H P_k^- H^T + R)^{-1}$

Measurement Update:
$\hat{x}_k = \hat{x}_k^- + K_k (z_k - H \hat{x}_k^-)$
$P_k = (I - K_k H) P_k^-$

Notice:
When $R \to 0$, $K \to H^{-1}$ (trust sensor completely).
When $R \to \infty$, $K \to 0$ (trust kinematic model completely).
Uncertainty ellipse shrinks monotonically to algebraic Riccati limit.
